# hyperfluid_group_member (Resource)

Adds a user or a service account to a `hyperfluid_group`; the member inherits every grant and role bound to the group. Requires `group:read` and `group:update`.

A public-client service account cannot be a member: it authenticates as the signed-in user, never as itself, so the API refuses it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Service accounts are created in the console or with hfctl; Terraform
# references them.
data "hyperfluid_service_account" "etl" {
  client_id = "etl"
}

variable "alice_user_id" {
  type = string
}

resource "hyperfluid_group_member" "alice" {
  group_id       = hyperfluid_group.data_eng.id
  principal_type = "user"
  principal_id   = var.alice_user_id
}

resource "hyperfluid_group_member" "etl" {
  group_id       = hyperfluid_group.data_eng.id
  principal_type = "service_account"
  principal_id   = data.hyperfluid_service_account.etl.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `group_id` (String) Id of the group. Changing this forces a new membership.
- `principal_id` (String) Id of the user, or of the service account (the `hyperfluid_service_account` data source's `id`, not its `client_id`). Users and service accounts are created in the console or with hfctl, never by Terraform. Changing this forces a new membership.
- `principal_type` (String) `user` or `service_account`. Changing this forces a new membership.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<group_id>/<principal_type>/<principal_id>`.
- `principal_name` (String) The user's email, or the service account's name.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import id is "<group_id>/<principal_type>/<principal_id>".
terraform import hyperfluid_group_member.alice 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/user/11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111
```
